skip_reason: Intake call for a 2,800 sqft two-story, 4-bedroom home (well over the 1,800 sqft walkthrough threshold). After gathering basic details and giving a partial hourly-rate/trip-fee overview, Roselyn routed the customer to a virtual walkthrough rather than finalizing pricing/clock/estimate on the call — those sections don't apply here pending Amanda/Cameron's walkthrough-scheduler mini-rubric decision.
top_strength: Roselyn stayed composed through a genuinely messy opening — a spam-number complaint, a misrouted inbox, and confusion over which branch owned the lead — and still got the customer's full home details, then smoothly pivoted him into a virtual walkthrough by texting the link and confirming he'd need to hang up to free his mic.
coaching_note: When John asked directly about the free travel zone and branch location, Roselyn's answer was shaky — she quoted 'ten to fifteen miles,' he pushed back with 'fifty miles,' and she then read out a Dallas address while also referencing a separate Garland branch without resolving which one applied to his move; on a lead who already distrusts the phone number as spam, she needs the trip-fee/branch-zone logic memorized cold so that answer lands as confident, not improvised.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient throughout (apologized for the wait, said 'sorry to hear that' to his spam complaint), but never used his name once and the call leaned transactional with repeated dead-air 'give me one sec' holds rather than warm back-and-forth.
